title: [Runner] Fix false-positive Win+Shift+C shortcut conflict on Windows 11

review.body_prefix:
### Qualified current-revision assessment

The Runner detector, header and hotkey regression-test inputs are byte-identical to the previously assessed revision. The additional change is in `ShutdownNotificationIsDeliveredBeforeSettingsHelperDisposal`: it now awaits `target.ShutdownReceived.Task` inside the helper lifetime, after `ShutdownAsync`, before disposal can close the pipe.

The target signals that completion only after recording `Shutdown`. The server is already running and observes the same completion task, so the new wait orders receipt before disposal rather than treating background-write queueing as delivery. It is bounded by the existing five-second wait and ten-second server cancellation; final cleanup still cancels/stops the server. No additional code correction is established by this scope review.

**Validation scope:** Exact Git-blob comparison covers all three Runner inputs. Earlier native detector/test compilation and the Windows 11 manager test remain evidence for their original revision, not newly executed current-revision checks. The changed managed test and its server/target lifetime were source-traced; the complete managed test project and CI retry were not independently executed. This is a qualified assessment, not an unconditional approval or a claim that the CI failures have cleared.

The latest maintainer approval is acknowledged on this unchanged head. An approval and a pipeline-start acknowledgment do not themselves establish a passing rerun.
